summary: The video side is a raster-driven pipeline. H/V counters address the tile RAM and graphics ROMs directly, and a per-line sprite machine scans sprite RAM and ORs pixels into ping-pong line buffers. A CPU-side sprite cache RAM is copied to the real sprite RAM during two lines after the visible area. The SSIO sound board is built from its counter chain (74161/74160/14024), a bit-serial 82S123 PROM and per-voice down-counters that gate the AY outputs. MAME collapses that board into a static volume table and a periodic timer. Nothing mirrors MAME's tilemap, its render_sprites loop or its device decomposition beyond the memory and I/O map that both must share.

findings.signal: scan-time tile fetch from raster counter bits
findings.note: The tile RAM address is vflip(8:4)&hcnt_flip(8:4), the ROM address is tile code & V3..V1 & H3, and the 2bpp planes are selected by hcnt(2:1) each pixel. MAME instead uses a 16x16 tilemap drawn per frame.

findings.signal: per-line sprite engine with ping-pong line buffers
findings.note: A phase-counter state machine checks all 128 sprites against the next line with an adder (sp_vcnt = vflip + ypos*2) and fetches 4 ROM bytes per hit. It writes them into one of two 256x8 line buffers, chosen by the V LSB, while the other buffer is read out and cleared. MAME instead draws each sprite's 32 rows into a frame bitmap.

findings.signal: sprite cache to sprite RAM transfer at fixed raster lines
findings.note: The CPU writes a staging RAM. A raster-decoded move_buf window (vcnt=500-501) copies it into a second RAM addressed by vcnt(0)&hcnt(8:1). MAME has a single spriteram with no such transfer.

findings.signal: line-buffer OR merge, transparency by zero nibble
findings.note: The buffer write data is the read-back value ORed with the ROM byte. Sprite-versus-background selection is sp_vid="0000" in a palette mux, which differs from MAME's pri bitmap and its (pix & 0x07) draw test.
CTC channel 3 is triggered by decoding vcnt=493 on alternate fields (top_frame), and ZC/TO0 is wired to TRG1 as a port connection. MAME pulses trg3 from a scanline-0 timer callback.

div_E11, div_D11 and div_C12 are a carry-chained binary, decade and ripple counter. The interrupt is the inverted bit 6 of C12, and a read in the E000 range resets it asynchronously. MAME models this with a periodic interrupt callback that increments a count variable.

findings.signal: duty-cycle modulation from bit-serial PROM and down-counters
findings.note: The 82S123 PROM is addressed by the D11/E11 count and shifted out bit by bit as a clock (74166-style). That clock decrements six 4-bit counters loaded from the AY ports, and each AY voice passes only while its counter is zero. MAME precomputes a static volume table from the same PROM.

findings.signal: AY bus control from address-line gating
findings.note: BDIR and BC1 are NOR-style gate equations of the chip select with A0 and A1, as discrete logic would drive the AY pins. They are not handler functions per register.

ROM, RAM, sprite, palette and video RAM ranges, the SSIO ports at 0x00-0x07 and 0x1C-0x1F, and the CTC at 0xF0 match MAME. The F400/F800 palette split matches MAME's xRBG_444 write8/write8_ext. Any correct core must share these.

Code is bits 5:0, hflip bit 6, vflip bit 7, and positions are doubled. These match MAME because they are register semantics. Flip is applied as XOR on ROM address bits and a nibble swap, not as MAME's loop-index XOR.
Clock enables are divided from 40MHz, and a progressive 31kHz mode and a synthesized 15kHz csync are added. This is ordinary FPGA engineering.
